title: KV cache iterator snapshot poisoning — root cause, containment, and long-term safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up ticket for the KV cache incident where concurrent iterator snapshots could observe and subsequently retain references to slab memory that was concurrently compacted or freed, leading to transient data corruption and potential cross-namespace contamination. This ticket tracks the RCA, short-term mitigations, and long-term runtime changes to eliminate the hazard window and prevent future poisoning vectors.
investigation_summary: Summary: A race between the iterator snapshot path and the background compaction/eviction worker was identified. Iterators capture a lightweight view (prefix index + pointer) without acquiring the stabilizing refcount on the slab. If compaction moved or freed the slab entry before the iterator materialized its value, the iterator could later reify stale pointers. In a subset of workloads that produce large numbers of small prefix mutations (observed during a synthetic stress test and a customer embed heavy batch), we saw pointer aliasing and occasional cross-namespace reads. Root cause points: 1) iterator snapshot is lock-free but doesn't pin slab memory; 2) compaction path assumes no active readers on entries older than epoch N but epoch tracking was coarse-grained; 3) eviction heuristics could prematurely recycle memory because of estimator inaccuracy. We validated with a deterministic repro harness that reproduces the stale-read within 10k ops on affected branches. No evidence of malicious intent was found — this is a race under high-concurrency mutation workloads.
timeline_of_actions:
2026-03-02: Incident begins with elevated error counts and customer reports of inconsistent embeddings.
2026-03-03: Pager escalation, triage, and short-term rollback of recently deployed iterator optimization.
2026-03-04: Containment: disabled aggressive compaction on affected clusters, temporarily increased grace-window TTL for slab reuse, and enabled additional checksum asserts.
2026-03-06: Deterministic repro harness created and run against current main; race reproduced.
2026-03-07: This follow-up ticket opened to track mitigations and engineering tasks.
2026-03-11: Proposed long-term fixes reviewed in design doc.
2026-03-13: PR for conservative iterator pin applied to internal canary cluster.
action_items: A: Add slab pinning to iterator snapshot path (owner: Liam O'Connor) — implement a lightweight refcount increment or hazard pointer so iterators hold live references until materialization. ETA: 2026-03-22
B: Replace coarse-grained epoch with per-namespace epoch counters in compaction (owner: Priya Raman) — reduces false-positive frees. ETA: 2026-04-05
C: Tighten eviction estimator to avoid premature slab reuse under bursty mutation workloads (owner: Marco Silva) — add decaying high-water mark and telemetry. ETA: 2026-03-29
D: Deploy checksum-on-read asserts in canary and stage for two weeks (owner: SRE Team) — will detect silent corruption earlier. ETA: 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-30
E: Add deterministic concurrency tests to CI (owner: Test Infra) — run iterator+compactor stress scenario nightly; add new flaky-test guard and a repro artifact. ETA: 2026-03-20
F: Instrument precise metric for 'iterator-stale-reify' events and a dashboard (owner: Observability) — correlate with compaction rate and mutation throughput. ETA: 2026-03-18
G: Communication: notify impacted customers with incident summary and next steps (owner: Customer Success) — message draft in Confluence. ETA: 2026-03-14
mitigation_timeline:
Short-term (already done): rolled back iterator optimization; increased slab grace window; enabled additional asserts and scheduled canary with conservative pins.
Medium-term (3 weeks): implement iterator pinning, CI tests, and monitoring.
Long-term (6-10 weeks): redesign compaction epoching, eviction heuristics, and consider persistent index versioning to make reify path idempotent.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Pinning slab entries increases memory pressure and could worsen OOM patterns in extreme workloads; we'll mitigate by making pinning lazy and bounded-per-iterator. Per-namespace epoch counters add metadata overhead and slight compaction latency but reduce false frees. Conservative default settings may increase tail latency; we plan to gate these changes behind canary and feature flags to profile cost/benefit.
acceptance_criteria:
1) No repro of stale reify in deterministic harness after iterator pinning and compaction epoch change.
2) Canary clusters run for 2 weeks with zero checksum-on-read failures.
3) CI nightly stress shows regression rate < 0.01% on iterator compaction scenarios.
4) Post-deploy telemetry shows acceptable memory tail (within 10% of pre-change baseline) and no customer-facing errors.
followup_notes: Note 2026-03-13: Initial pinning PR merged to canary; we saw a 1.8x increase in resident set for canary hosts under synthetic workload — follow-up tuning required.

Note 2026-03-10: Security review deemed not required as no exfiltration vector was identified; still document the hazard for compliance audits.
